title: Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?
text:
Abstract
In a complete theory there is an element corresponding to each element of reality. A sufficient condition for the reality of a physical quantity is the possibility of predicting it with certainty, without disturbing the system. In quantum mechanics in the case of two physical quantities described by non-commuting operators, the knowledge of one precludes the knowledge of the other. Then either (1) the description of reality given by the wave function in quantum mechanics is not complete or (2) these two quantities cannot have simultaneous reality. Consideration of the problem of making predictions concerning a system on the basis of measurements made on another system that had previously interacted with it leads to the result that if (1) is false then (2) is also false. One is thus led to conclude that the description of reality as given by a wave function is not complete.

title: Econ 47503: Forecasting
text:
Course Description:
Elementary forecasting techniques and econometric models are introduced in this course. Students will learn the skills to do business forecasting, to estimate different econometric models, to compare forecasting models, and to do basic regression analysis with time series data. All empirical analysis is based on software such as Microsoft Excel, EViews and Stata.

title: Econ 44303: Experimental Economics
text:
Course Description:
The course offers an introduction to the field of experimental economics. Covered topics include market competition, asset market bubbles, auction design, bargaining and behavioral labor economics, information and signaling. Students will get a deeper understanding of these important concepts via participating in experiments as players, conducting experiments in class and even designing their own experiments, and analyzing experimental data. Experiments can engage students to reflect on what they learned in class about economic theory, and the goal of the class is to help students approach problems in an analytical framework and think more critically.

Course Description:
Economics of Organizations prepares students to estimate and define the relationship between key economic variables which affect the performance of a firm. Rooted in Microeconomic Theory, Economics of Organizations examines those factors that influence the decision making process of a firm. Knowledge of how to interpret graphs, algebra, calculus and statistics are essential elements necessary for this pursuit.

title: Econ 39303: Seminar on the Japanese Economic System
text: Prerequisites:

title: Econ 39303: Seminar on the Japanese Economic System
text:
Course Description:
This class presents essential facts about the Japanese economy and then subjects these facts to modern economic analyses, both theoretical and empirical. Japanese institutions and policies are contrasted with their American counterparts, and the two countries’ economies are compared in terms of performance. Relevant aspects of Japan’s history, culture and politics are explored in order to gain a better understanding of contemporary business practices. Current issues including US-Japanese trade conflicts, the Japanese distribution system and asset prices (land and equities) are also examined.

title: Econ 38403: Economic Development, Poverty & the Role of the World Bank and IMF in Low-Income Countries
text:
Course Description:
This course examines theories and patterns of economic development in emerging economies and the role of the World Bank and IMF in low-income countries. The first section of the course provides an introduction to development economics and follows the text fairly closely. The second section focuses on the World Bank and IMF and has two subsections. The first examines the World Bank and IMF history, their contemporary roles, and their successes and failures in fostering development and stability. The second consists of team projects entailing the in-depth study of a specific World Bank Lending Program or an IMF Structural Adjustment Program; each team presents its findings to the class during the final two weeks of the semester.

This course focuses on the employment relationship, in other words, the interaction of employers and employees. The objective of this course is to develop the analytical skills necessary to understand the incentives that influence the behavior of employers and employees. Everyone is an employee or employer or both for a significant portion of their life. A study of the incentives that influence the decisions of individuals in either of these roles can be valuable regardless of one’s intended occupation.

title: Econ 30503: Economics for Elementary Teachers
text:
Course Description:
This course is designed to:

teach economic concepts;
demonstrate effective techniques for teaching these concepts to your future students;
familiarize you with national economics standards and Arkansas social studies frameworks; and

Course Description:
This is an intermediate level course about microeconomics, the branch of economics dealing with household and firm behavior. In this course, we will analyze how consumers and firms make decisions and how the details of the marketplace can affect the allocation of resources. There will be a special focus on those situations where the market fails to provide good outcomes, and we will discuss what steps can be taken to restore efficiency. Whenever possible, the course focuses on aspects of business decision making, such as price discrimination, advertising, and business strategy.

title: Econ 44203: Behavioral Economics
text:
Prerequisites:
Students are assumed to be familiar with common optimization techniques (taking derivatives); calculus is reviewed at the beginning of the course.

title: Econ 44203: Behavioral Economics
text:
Course Description:
This course examines some basic assumptions about human behavior common in economics (people are purely self-interested; can do statistics really well; have preferences only over final outcomes; exponentially discount the future; have well-defined and stable preferences, and more). It investigates how these assumptions came to be, their benefits and shortcomings, and how understanding psychology can lead to better assumptions and more realistic economic models. Like all economics, the course tries to understand the driving forces of economic behavior, but it spends a great amount of time looking at lab experiments to find whether observed behavior is consistent with the assumptions being used, and strives to incorporate a richer, more realistic set of assumptions into our models.

title: Econ 46303: International Trade
text:
Prerequisites:
Familiarity with the material in ECON 21003 (Principles of Macroeconomics) and ECON 22003 (Principles of Microeconomics), or ECON 21403 (Basic Economics: Theory and Practice).

title: Econ 46303: International Trade
text:
Course Description:
This class covers the basic concepts, models, new explanations and policies for international trade. We will learn three core models in this course: the Ricardian model, the Specific-factors model and the Heckscher-Ohlin model. In addition to the conventional trade topics, some new explanations and real applications for international trade will also be covered. Based on these theories, we will discuss trade policy: tariffs, quotas and subsidies, and the impact of trade policies on the patterns of trade and on the welfare of countries.

title: Econ 47403: Introduction to Econometrics
text:
Prerequisites:
Principles of economics (ECON 21003 and ECON 22003, or ECON 21403), calculus (MATH 2043 or MATH 2555), quantitative analysis (ECON 4733 or MATH 2053) and statistics (CISQ 2013).

title: Econ 47403: Introduction to Econometrics
text:
Course Description:
Introduction to the application of statistical methods to economic problems. This course covers basic econometric methods. The most important part of the course is learning how to set up and solve econometric problems. Problem sets give practice in using the methods studied in class, and some involve the use of computers.

title: Econ 47403: Introduction to Econometrics
text:
Value of the Course:
Econometrics gives empirical content to most economic theory. In this course you will learn how to test economic theories using real data and how to determine the validity of your tests. This knowledge will help you to use economic theory to formulate and/or assess business and public policy decisions.
